gen-dafont-origami-gf-noto-sans-lisu: Single-stroke brush lettering, heavy as poured lead. Origami is the one that grabs attention with its constant-width swagger, while Noto Sans Lisu does the quiet work of staying readable, with generous s curves.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-saira: Hollow glass-tube lettering, drawn at constant width. Origami supplies the showy tube-light outline, while Saira, a sans-serif with rounded letters reaching high, keeps a visible gap in every s.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-sarpanch: Cord-like curves, brushed in one stroke. Sarpanch keeps things approachable, its e clearly open and its ascenders tucked close, so a whole page of it moves along easily while Origami stays the showpiece.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-sulphur-point: Marker-bold curves with a lead-type heft. Origami's constant-width brush stroke meets Sulphur Point, a sans with bulky proportions and distinct gaps, and the shared marker-like weight is what ties them.
